newsitem.title: USA: Kohl expects Russia to host G8 in future.
newsitem.headline: Kohl expects Russia to host G8 in future.

text.p: Russia is now part of the group known as the Group of Seven leading industrialized nations and will at some stage host a summit of an expanded eight-nation group, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Sunday.
"I am sure that Russia will be the host, although I would not like to pin myself down on a date," Kohl told a news conference after this year's annual G7 summit in Denver, Colorado.
Russia, an invited guest at G7 summits since 1991, attended almost all of the discussions in Denver and it was dubbed the "Summit of the Eight".
The omnipresence of Russian president Boris Yeltsin at the talks -- with the exception of a brief economic session -- led to talk that the group had in effect turned into a Group oif Eight.
Kohl avoided using this terminology in his opening remarks at the news conference, saying: "The process of the integration of Russia was continued. Yeltsin was present from the start.
"One can debate whether Russia has been admitted fully or 90 percent. The fact is that he (Yeltsin) was there, this is the reality and it is a sensible one."

The first economic summit of the leading industrialized countries was held in Rambouillet, France, in 1975, with six countries participating -- Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.
Canada and the European Community joined the talks in 1977, although the European grouping has never been accorded the status of full membership.
Asked whether Germany could pave the way for Russia to host its first full annual summit meeting by inviting Moscow to take Bonn's place in the rotation in 1999, Kohl responded cautiously.
"It is interesting that you ask this because it means I should build it into my thinking immediately," he quipped. "But for now I would say that it is unlikely."
